Topics · Meaning and purpose

Is my wealth really mine?

The Quran protects ownership, honours earning, and calls wealth a trust with a right in it for others.

Part 1 of 3

﴿ءَامِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَأَنفِقُوا۟ مِمَّا جَعَلَكُم مُّسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ ۖ فَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ مِنكُمْ وَأَنفَقُوا۟ لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Believe in Allāh and His Messenger and spend out of that in which He has made you successive inheritors. For those who have believed among you and spent,[1629] there will be a great reward.

Translator's notes

[1629] In ways pleasing to Allāh.

Quran · Al-Hadid 57:7

Give to the Most High according as he has given. As your hand has found, give generously. For the Lord repays, and he will repay you sevenfold.

Sirach · 35:10-11

World English Bible

Where did your money come from? From your effort, yes. But who gave you the body that worked, the mind that planned, the country that allowed it, the year it went well? The verse does not deny your effort. It adds something: spend from what He has entrusted to you. You hold it now; it was in other hands before you and will be in others after. The sharper question is: is it yours forever?

A question for you

What brought you what you have?

If you sayMy effort.
ThenFair, and the Quran honours earning. The verse only asks about what came before your effort.
If you sayChances I did not make.
ThenThen you see what the verse sees.
If you sayI do not have much.
ThenThe verse does not measure by quantity. What you have, however little, is a trust and a dignity.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَٱبْتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ ۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۖ وَأَحْسِن كَمَآ أَحْسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ ۖ وَلَا تَبْغِ ٱلْفَسَادَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ٧٧ قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِندِىٓ ۚ أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ مَنْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُ قُوَّةً وَأَكْثَرُ جَمْعًا ۚ وَلَا يُسْـَٔلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ٧٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

But seek, through that which Allāh has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allāh has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allāh does not like corrupters." He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Did he not know that Allāh had destroyed before him of generations those who were greater than him in power and greater in accumulation [of wealth]? But the criminals, about their sins, will not be asked.[1119]

Translator's notes

[1119] There will be no need to enumerate their sins separately, as their quantity is obvious and more than sufficient to warrant punishment in Hell.

Quran · Al-Qasas 28:77-78

Translation

He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly. He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’ He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods. I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.”’ “But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’ So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”

Original · Ancient Greek

εἶπεν δὲ παραβολὴν πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων· Ἀνθρώπου τινὸς πλουσίου εὐφόρησεν ἡ χώρα. καὶ διελογίζετο ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Τί ποιήσω, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχω ποῦ συνάξω τοὺς καρπούς μου; καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτο ποιήσω· καθελῶ μου τὰς ἀποθήκας καὶ μείζονας οἰκοδομήσω, καὶ συνάξω ἐκεῖ πάντα τὸν σῖτον καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά μου, καὶ ἐρῶ τῇ ψυχῇ μου· Ψυχή, ἔχεις πολλὰ ἀγαθὰ κείμενα εἰς ἔτη πολλά· ἀναπαύου, φάγε, πίε, εὐφραίνου. εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ θεός· Ἄφρων, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τὴν ψυχήν σου ἀπαιτοῦσιν ἀπὸ σοῦ· ἃ δὲ ἡτοίμασας, τίνι ἔσται; οὕτως ὁ θησαυρίζων ἑαυτῷ καὶ μὴ εἰς θεὸν πλουτῶν.

the Gospel (Luke) · 12:16-21

World English Bible

Wealth tests a person with one word: from where? Qarun's people offer balanced advice: seek the next life with what you have, do not forget your share of this world, do good as God has done good to you. Wealth itself is not the problem. His reply reveals the matter: I was given it by knowledge I have. Once money becomes proof of the self, it stops being a trust. The difference between the two positions is one sentence.

A question for you

Which piece of advice in the verse reaches you most?

If you sayDo not forget your share of this world.
ThenIt is good that this is in the text. Enjoyment is part of the road.
If you sayDo good as God has done good to you.
ThenThen giving is a kind of returning. The next part asks what the poor are owed.
If you sayWhy would a blessing be a test at all?
ThenA good question, with its own Step.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَفِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ حَقٌّ لِّلسَّآئِلِ وَٱلْمَحْرُومِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And from their properties was [given] the right of the [needy] petitioner and the deprived.

Quran · Adh-Dhariyat 51:19

Translation

If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also. Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two. Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ τῷ θέλοντί σοι κριθῆναι καὶ τὸν χιτῶνά σου λαβεῖν, ἄφες αὐτῷ καὶ τὸ ἱμάτιον· καὶ ὅστις σε ἀγγαρεύσει μίλιον ἕν, ὕπαγε μετʼ αὐτοῦ δύο. τῷ αἰτοῦντί σε δός, καὶ τὸν θέλοντα ἀπὸ σοῦ δανίσασθαι μὴ ἀποστραφῇς.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 5:40-42

World English Bible

If giving were pure favour, the poor would owe the rich their thanks. The verse turns this round with one word: in their wealth there is a right. A right is paid, and it is not held over anyone. On this reading part of what is in your account is another's due, deposited with you. That keeps the dignity of the poor, and frees the wealthy from imagining they are the benefactor.

A question for you

To you, what is the difference between a favour and a right?

If you sayA right is not held over anyone.
ThenThat is the dignity of the poor.
If you sayA favour is more beautiful.
ThenGenerosity beyond what is owed has a wide place in the Quran, and 92:20 describes it.
If you sayI am not convinced the poor have a right in my money.
ThenMany hold that view. The question remains: where did your ability come from, and why you and not another?

The same in the other books

Translation

Yahweh says, “Don’t let the wise man glory in his wisdom. Don’t let the mighty man glory in his might. Don’t let the rich man glory in his riches. But let him who glories glory in this, that he has understanding, and knows me, that I am Yahweh who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness on the earth, for I delight in these things,” says Yahweh.
